passage_parts.label: A
passage_parts.title: Text A: A Letter to the Editor from a Venetian
passage_parts.text: I was born in Venice, and I have watched my neighbors leave one by one as their homes were turned into places for tourists to stay. Fewer than 50,000 people now live in the old city, yet about 20 million visitors came in 2023 alone, and roughly half of them did not even stay the night. So I was glad when, in 2024, Venice became the first city in the world to make day-trippers pay just to walk in. On 29 of the busiest days, most people arriving just for the day had to buy a €5 ticket online. Critics called this an attack on the freedom to travel. I call it a modest first step. Visitors who sleep in the city do not pay, since they already pay a tax on each night of their stay. In 2025, the fee covered 54 days, and anyone who booked fewer than four days ahead paid €10. Even so, the crowds have hardly thinned. The city must charge more, and it must protect homes for the people who keep Venice alive.

passage_parts.label: B
passage_parts.title: Text B: A Day-Tripper’s Travel Blog
passage_parts.text: In May 2025, I was staying with friends in Padua, a short train ride from Venice, and on Friday evening we suddenly decided to spend that Sunday there. Sunday turned out to be one of the fee days, so I booked my ticket online that night and saved the QR code on my phone. Nobody ever asked to see it. To be honest, the fee bothers me. Hotels in Venice are far beyond my budget, which is exactly why I came for the day, and yet guests in those hotels never buy a ticket at all. It feels as if the city welcomes tourists with money and charges the rest of us for being careful with ours. And did the fee make Venice any quieter? Not that I could tell. By mid-morning, the streets near the Rialto Bridge were so packed that I could barely move. I agree that something must be done, but making visitors pay more is not the answer. Perhaps the city should help people spread their visits across the year instead.

questions.stem: What are the two texts mainly about?

options.A: How visitors can book a ticket for Venice online.
options.B: Two views on making day visitors pay to enter Venice.
options.C: Why so many people have moved out of Venice.
options.D: The best time of year for a trip to Venice.

questions.stem: What does “this” in Text A refer to?

options.A: Choosing only the 29 busiest days of the year for the fee.
options.B: Selling all of the tickets on the internet instead of at gates.
options.C: Making people who come just for the day pay to enter.
options.D: Neighbors leaving their homes in the old city one by one.

questions.stem: Based on both texts, how much did the writer of Text B most likely pay to enter Venice?

options.A: Nothing, since the writer spent the night in a nearby city.
options.B: €5, since the ticket was bought online in advance.
options.C: €5, since the visit fell on a Sunday.
options.D: €10, since the ticket was booked two days ahead.

questions.stem: Which of the following can be inferred about the two writers?

options.A: Both doubt that the charge has eased the crowding so far.
options.B: Both would like to see day visitors charged a higher fee.
options.C: The writer of Text A thinks hotel guests should pay the fee too.
options.D: The writer of Text B was fined for not showing a ticket.

1.explanation_zh: 文本 A 是威尼斯居民的投書，支持向一日遊旅客收入城費，認為收費太低、還應該加價並保護居民住宅；文本 B 是一日遊旅客的部落格，覺得這筆費用不公平、加價不是辦法。兩篇談的是同一件事——向一日遊旅客收入城費——但立場不同，所以是 B。
evidence: So I was glad when, in 2024, Venice became the first city in the world to make day-trippers pay just to walk in.
To be honest, the fee bothers me.
I agree that something must be done, but making visitors pay more is not the answer.

option_notes_zh.A: 線上訂票、存 QR code 只是兩篇提到的細節，不是主要內容。
option_notes_zh.C: 居民搬離舊城只出現在文本 A 開頭，是作者支持收費的理由之一；文本 B 完全沒提，不能涵蓋兩篇。
option_notes_zh.D: 兩篇都沒有討論一年中什麼時候最適合去威尼斯；文本 B 最後只建議把遊客分散到一年各個時候。

1.strategy_zh: 多文本的主旨題要找「兩篇共同討論的主題」，再看兩篇的立場是否不同；只出現在其中一篇的內容不是答案。
hints: 文本 A 的作者對入城費的態度是什麼？
文本 B 的作者對入城費的態度是什麼？
兩篇共同在討論哪一項措施？

C: I was born in Venice, and I have watched my neighbors leave one by one as their homes were turned into places for tourists to stay.

2.explanation_zh: this 前兩句說：2024 年威尼斯成為全世界第一個讓一日遊旅客「光是走進城就要付費」的城市，在 29 個最擁擠的日子，大多數當天來回的人都要上網買 5 歐元的票。批評者說 this 是「對旅行自由的攻擊」，作者則說它是「溫和的第一步」——被批評、被辯護的都是「向只待一天的人收入城費」這件事。
evidence: So I was glad when, in 2024, Venice became the first city in the world to make day-trippers pay just to walk in.
On 29 of the busiest days, most people arriving just for the day had to buy a €5 ticket online.
Critics called this an attack on the freedom to travel.

option_notes_zh.A: 「挑出最擁擠的日子」只是收費制度的一部分，本身不會被說成「攻擊旅行自由」；限制旅行自由的是收費這件事。
option_notes_zh.B: online 只是買票的方式；代回原句「批評者說上網售票是對旅行自由的攻擊」說不通。
option_notes_zh.D: 居民搬走是作者在開頭描述的現象，不是批評者批評的對象。

2.strategy_zh: 指涉題把選項代回原句「Critics called ＿＿ an attack on the freedom to travel. I call it a modest first step.」，兩句都要說得通。
hints: this 前面兩句說威尼斯開始做什麼？
什麼樣的措施會被批評為「攻擊旅行自由」？
作者說「溫和的第一步」，指的是什麼措施？

B: On 29 of the busiest days, most people arriving just for the day had to buy a €5 ticket online.

3.explanation_zh: 文本 A 說明 2025 年的規則：在四天內才訂票的人要付 10 歐元，住在城裡過夜的人才不用付。文本 B 的作者 2025 年 5 月住在帕多瓦（不是威尼斯城內），星期五晚上才決定星期天去，當晚訂票，只提前兩天。綜合兩篇，作者最可能付了 10 歐元。
evidence: In 2025, the fee covered 54 days, and anyone who booked fewer than four days ahead paid €10.
Visitors who sleep in the city do not pay, since they already pay a tax on each night of their stay.
In May 2025, I was staying with friends in Padua, a short train ride from Venice, and on Friday evening we suddenly decided to spend that Sunday there.
Sunday turned out to be one of the fee days, so I booked my ticket online that night and saved the QR code on my phone.

option_notes_zh.A: 免費的是「住在威尼斯城內」過夜的人；作者住在附近的帕多瓦，仍然算一日遊旅客。
option_notes_zh.B: 線上訂票是所有一日遊旅客都要做的事，不會因此變成 5 歐元；5 歐元要提前四天以上訂。
option_notes_zh.C: 票價取決於提前幾天訂票，不是星期幾；而且作者星期五晚上才訂、星期天就去。

3.strategy_zh: 跨文本題要把一篇的「規則」套到另一篇的「人物情況」：先在文本 A 找出收費規則與例外，再到文本 B 找作者住哪裡、哪天訂票、哪天去。
hints: 文本 A 說 2025 年什麼情況要付 10 歐元？什麼人不用付？
文本 B 的作者住在哪裡？是威尼斯城內嗎？
作者哪天訂票、哪天去？提前了幾天？

A: Visitors who sleep in the city do not pay, since they already pay a tax on each night of their stay.
In May 2025, I was staying with friends in Padua, a short train ride from Venice, and on Friday evening we suddenly decided to spend that Sunday there.

4.explanation_zh: 文本 A 的作者說「即使如此，人潮幾乎沒有變少」，還說 5 歐元太少；文本 B 的作者問收費有沒有讓威尼斯安靜一點，自己回答「我看不出來」，上午就擠得動彈不得。兩人立場雖然不同，但都覺得目前為止收費並沒有讓人潮減少，所以是 A。
evidence: Even so, the crowds have hardly thinned.
And did the fee make Venice any quieter? Not that I could tell.
By mid-morning, the streets near the Rialto Bridge were so packed that I could barely move.

option_notes_zh.B: 只有文本 A 的作者主張收更多錢；文本 B 的作者明說「讓遊客付更多錢不是辦法」，兩人在這一點正好相反。
option_notes_zh.C: 文本 A 的作者說明住宿旅客已經付了每晚的住宿稅，所以不用付入城費，並沒有主張他們也要付。
option_notes_zh.D: 文本 B 的作者說從頭到尾沒有人要求看票，不可能因為沒出示票被罰。

4.strategy_zh: 比較兩位作者時，先分別寫下兩人的立場（支持或反對、想怎麼改），再找兩人「同意」的地方；只有一人主張的選項不能說成兩人都這樣想。
hints: 文本 A 的作者對收費後的人潮怎麼說？
文本 B 的作者覺得收費讓威尼斯變安靜了嗎？
兩人對「加價」的看法一樣嗎？

B: The city must charge more, and it must protect homes for the people who keep Venice alive.
I agree that something must be done, but making visitors pay more is not the answer.
C: Visitors who sleep in the city do not pay, since they already pay a tax on each night of their stay.
D: Nobody ever asked to see it.

translation_zh.text:
威尼斯的入城費

文本 A：一位威尼斯居民的投書

我在威尼斯出生，眼看著鄰居一個接一個離開，他們的房子被改成給觀光客住的地方。現在住在舊城區的人不到五萬，可是光是 2023 年就來了大約兩千萬名遊客，其中大約一半甚至沒有留下來過夜。所以 2024 年威尼斯成為全世界第一個讓一日遊旅客「光是走進城就要付錢」的城市時，我很高興。在 29 個最擁擠的日子裡，大多數只待一天的人都必須上網買一張 5 歐元的票。批評的人說這是對旅行自由的攻擊；我則說這是溫和的第一步。在城裡過夜的遊客不必付費，因為他們每住一晚都已經付了稅。2025 年，收費日增加到 54 天，而在四天內才訂票的人要付 10 歐元。即使如此，人潮幾乎沒有變少。市政府必須收更多錢，也必須為讓威尼斯維持生命力的居民保住住處。

文本 B：一位一日遊旅客的旅遊部落格

2025 年 5 月，我住在帕多瓦的朋友家，從那裡搭火車到威尼斯很近。星期五晚上我們突然決定那個星期天去威尼斯。那個星期天正好是收費日之一，所以我當晚就上網訂票，把 QR code 存在手機裡。結果從頭到尾都沒有人要求看。老實說，這筆費用讓我很不舒服。威尼斯的旅館遠遠超出我的預算，這正是我只來一天的原因；可是住在那些旅館裡的客人根本不用買票。感覺上，這座城市歡迎有錢的觀光客，卻向我們這些精打細算的人收錢。那麼，收費有沒有讓威尼斯安靜一點？我是看不出來。到了上午過半，里亞托橋附近的街道已經擠得我幾乎動彈不得。我同意總得做點什麼，但讓遊客付更多錢不是辦法。也許市政府應該幫助大家把參觀時間分散到一年中的不同時候。

open_tasks.prompt: Fill in a table comparing the two writers: (1) their opinion of the fee, (2) one reason they give, and (3) what they think the city should do. Then write one English sentence saying which writer you agree with more and why.
reference_answers: Text A: supports the fee / too many day-trippers and residents are leaving / charge more and protect homes. Text B: dislikes the fee / it is unfair to visitors on a budget / help people spread their visits across the year. I agree more with Text B, because spreading visits out could reduce crowds without punishing people who cannot afford hotels.
I agree more with the writer of Text A, because Venice cannot survive as a real city if its residents keep moving away.
checklist_zh: 表格的三欄（立場、理由、建議）兩位作者都有填
填的內容都能在文中找到根據
最後一句有清楚表明同意哪一位
理由完整、是正確的英文句子

1.explanation_zh: A 文支持向一日遊客收費，B 文對此不滿，兩篇是對同一政策的兩種看法。

Sunday turned out to be one of the fee days, so I booked my ticket online that night and saved the QR code on my phone.

checked.claim: 2024 年威尼斯成為全球第一個向一日遊旅客收入城費的城市（ABC/Reuters、France 24）
2024 年在 29 天收費、5 歐元、線上登記取得 QR code（ABC、France 24）
在城內過夜的旅客已付住宿稅，不需付入城費（AFP 2025：Overnight visitors, who already pay a tourist tax, are exempt）
2025 年收費日 54 天；四天前訂 5 歐元、三天內才訂 10 歐元（AFP 2025）
舊城區居民不到五萬（France 24：below 50,000 in the historic center；ABC：around 49,000）
2023 年約兩千萬名遊客，約一半沒有過夜（ABC：some 20 million … roughly half）
